chunks: From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuha and Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who was known, virtuous, who died and left upon him a debt that he had been tested with, who was not a squanderer, nor a beggar known for asking, is one thousand and two thousand paid from the zakat on his behalf? He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Can zakat be used to pay off the debts of a deceased person?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that zakat funds can be used to settle the debts of a deceased, virtuous individual who was not known for begging or extravagance, highlighting the principle of 'qada' al-duyun' (paying off debts) as a primary category of zakat recipients. This ruling underscores the communal responsibility to preserve the dignity of the deceased and clear their financial obligations, even after death, provided they were not debtors by choice or negligence. The specific mention of amounts (one or two thousand dinars) reflects the economic context of the time and the flexibility in applying zakat to varying scales of debt.
